James Barr's "The Semantics of Biblical Language" was published in 1961 and is a seminal work in biblical studies and linguistics, critiquing simplistic/overly literal approaches to biblical language and rejecting the idea of a distinct static "biblical Hebrew" or "biblical Greek". #biblical-interpretation #james-barr

Main premise of Barr's "The Semantics of Biblical Language": a nuanced, contextualized understanding of biblical language is essential; language is fluid and contextual, so word meanings must be studied in historical/cultural context. #james-barr #biblical-interpretation

Page citations I gave for Barr's book (2023/05/21 chat): p.23 on meanings not existing in a vacuum and changing over time; p.44 on needing a word's entire range of usage including figurative senses; p.95 on idioms requiring cultural/historical context.
